title: A Border for the Safehouse
premise: Cyrus Sterling, a disgraced analyst hidden for two decades in a network of agency safe houses, discovers her current refuge listed on a real estate site with interior photos — including the wall of red string she thought only existed in her head. The listing is a message: someone inside the service knows she's alive and is flushing her out. Tasked with extracting a Russian defector before a Geneva summit, Cyrus realizes the defector may be bait designed to draw out every ghost like herself. She must choose between obeying the handler who once burned her and trusting the defector's claim that the sale listing was planted by the deputy director who erased her identity in the first place. In the end, Cyrus trades her own invisibility to expose him, walking out of the summit as herself — named, visible, and finally free.
about_author: Yara Halloran is the pen name of a former intelligence contractor turned novelist who writes from a farmhouse whose location she refuses to disclose. Her thrillers are known for bureaucratic dread, quiet love stories, and protagonists who know too much about how files get made.

chapters.title: The House That Isn't Hers
chapters.summary: Cyrus Sterling's POV. Scrolling listings at 3 a.m., she finds her safe house photographed room by room — down to the chipped mug she drinks from. Panic and disbelief; twenty years of protocol collapse in one browser tab. Emotional beat: the vertigo of being seen.

chapters.title: Protocol Nine
chapters.summary: Cyrus follows emergency procedure: burn evidence, relocate, report nothing. But her dead-drop returns a note in her old training cipher — known to only three people, one presumed dead. POV: Cyrus. Beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Handler Who Buried Me
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Cyrus's POV. Twenty years earlier: her recruitment by handler Elias Voss, the operation that 'killed' her, and the first rule — no attachments. Introduces the wound that explains every choice since. Beat: tender, elegiac.

chapters.title: Extraction Order
chapters.summary: Present day. Voss resurfaces with an order: extract defector Anya Reznik from Vienna before the Geneva summit. Cyrus suspects the timing isn't coincidence. POV alternates Cyrus/Voss. Beat: wary reunion between two people who owe each other everything and trust each other with nothing.

chapters.title: Anya
chapters.summary: Vienna. Cyrus observes the defector — brilliant, reckless, ordering dessert at a café she should have fled hours ago. First contact goes sideways when Anya says, 'You're the woman from the photographs.' POV: Cyrus. Beat: the ground tilts again.

chapters.title: What the Listing Sold
chapters.summary: Anya reveals she was shown the safe house photos as proof of Cyrus's existence — leverage to make her defect. Someone sold Cyrus's life as currency. POV: Anya. Beat: fury and reluctant kinship between two women used as assets.

chapters.title: The Third Name
chapters.summary: Cyrus works the cipher note backward. Three people knew it: Voss, her presumed-dead partner Marek, and Deputy Director Ilse Brandt — the architect of her erasure. POV: Cyrus. Beat: cold clarity; the hunt has a shape now.

chapters.title: Safe House Two
chapters.summary: The pair holes up in a secondary refuge that Cyrus finds also listed online — photos taken last week. The mole is close, feeding real-time intel. POV: Anya. Beat: claustrophobia, and the first unguarded conversation between them over canned peaches.

chapters.title: Marek's Grave
chapters.summary: Cyrus visits the empty grave where Marek Solin was supposedly buried and finds fresh flowers. Either he's alive or someone is taunting her. POV: Cyrus. Beat: grief reopened, hope she doesn't dare hold.

chapters.title: Voss's Ledger
chapters.summary: Voss intercepts them, wounded, carrying a ledger of every ghost asset Brandt has created and spent. He admits he wrote the cipher note — but not the listing. POV: Voss. Beat: confession without absolution; loyalty and betrayal indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Rules Rewritten
chapters.summary: Brandt's counter-move: Cyrus is officially designated a rogue asset, kill-on-sight. The machinery she served turns its guns toward her. POV: interagency comms, then Cyrus reading her own termination order. Beat: the loneliness of being paperwork.

chapters.title: The Peaches Again
chapters.summary: Quiet middle chapter. Anya and Cyrus trade histories in a cellar — Anya's daughter left behind in Moscow, Cyrus's twenty years of borrowed names. Something unnamed settles between them. POV: alternating. Beat: love arriving without permission.

chapters.title: Marek Lives
chapters.summary: Marek contacts Cyrus directly: he faked his death under Brandt's orders and can prove the listing came from Brandt's office — but he wants the ledger as payment. POV: Marek. Beat: hope priced in betrayal.

chapters.title: The Trade That Wasn't
chapters.summary: The handoff is ambushed — Marek set them up, or was set up. Voss takes a bullet covering their escape. POV: Cyrus. Beat: rage and guilt; the cost of trusting anyone, even family.

chapters.title: Interrogating the Dead
chapters.summary: With Voss dying, Cyrus finally asks the question she's avoided for twenty years: did he choose her because she was good, or because she was expendable? His answer reframes everything. POV: Voss's last hours. Beat: devastating tenderness.

chapters.title: Geneva Bound
chapters.summary: Anya proposes the unthinkable: walk into the summit itself, where Brandt will be, using the defector's scheduled debrief as cover. Cyrus must decide whether duty means delivering Anya or standing beside her. POV: Anya. Beat: resolve crystallizing into love declared plainly.

chapters.title: Summit Perimeter
chapters.summary: Infiltration through conference security using credentials from Voss's ledger. Taut procedural tension; near-misses with kill teams hunting Cyrus. POV: Cyrus. Beat: adrenaline laced with grief for Voss.

chapters.title: The Room Where I Was Erased
chapters.summary: Cyrus confronts Brandt mid-summit, broadcasting the ledger and the listing metadata to allied delegations. Brandt counters with Cyrus's own file — every sin committed in service. POV: Cyrus. Beat: the climax; visibility as both weapon and wound.

chapters.title: Bait Confirmed
chapters.summary: Brandt's plan unravels publicly: the defector program was a laundering scheme for compromised assets, and Anya was meant to be its final casualty. Marek, watching from the gallery, releases the proof he'd withheld. POV: Marek. Beat: partial redemption, bought late.

chapters.title: Kill Order Rescinded
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, Cyrus is offered reinstatement under a new name — the same old bargain. She looks at Anya and declines. POV: Cyrus. Beat: the quietest, hardest victory.

chapters.title: A Border for the Safehouse
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Cyrus and Anya cross into Slovenia and buy a house — openly, under Cyrus's real name, first time in twenty years. A border crossed not to hide but to arrive. POV: Cyrus. Beat: homecoming; identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: Appendix: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Coda of redacted documents, cipher notes, and the original real estate listing — letting readers reconstruct the conspiracy themselves. Final image: the photo of the chipped mug, captioned simply 'sold.' Beat: lingering unease beneath the happy ending.
